text:
alex.g: quick question — noticed inconsistent behavior for the `metadata` map on POST /v1/predict. py-sdk sends `null` when you pass an empty dict, ts-sdk omits the field when `undefined`. downstream validator treats null as an explicit value and rejects it. anyone else seen this?

maria: yep saw it in a customer report yesterday. they send `{}` in their UI, our python client turns that into `null` in the JSON body. fail mode is `400 invalid metadata` from the validation layer.

ben_engineer: minimal repro from my side:
```python
# py-sdk v1.4.2
body = {"input": "hi", "metadata": {}}
resp = client.predict.create(body)
# outgoing HTTP body: {"input":"hi","metadata":null}
```

sam_p: and TS?

ben_engineer: TS example:
```ts
// ts-sdk v0.21.0
const body = { input: 'hi', metadata: undefined }
client.predict.create(body)
// outgoing HTTP body: {"input":"hi"} // metadata omitted
```

alex.g: so three behaviors across stack: explicit `{}` -> `null` (py), omitted (ts), and server expects either object or omitted but rejects null. API contract in openapi.yaml says `metadata?: object` (nullable: false). I think server should treat `null` as invalid per contract, but SDKs should be consistent.

maria: agree. if the schema is not `nullable` we should not emit `null`. py-sdk probably has a serializer that maps empty mapping to None.

ben_engineer: quick trace — code path in py-sdk serializer uses `or None` somewhere when converting empty dicts to JSON. PR incoming. but before I push: should py emit `{}` for empty dicts or omit the field like TS?

sam_p: leaning toward always emitting object for typed maps (so `{}`), because omission loses intent in some workflows (customer distinguishes no-key vs empty metadata). but we should follow openapi semantics. openapi says property is optional; if user provides the value they expect it to appear even if empty. so TS omitting when undefined is ok, but if user passes `{}` explicitly TS will send `{}` right? we need to ensure that.

alex.g: good catch — in TS if you set `metadata: {}` it sends `{}`. the omission only happens when the field is `undefined`. The bug is py turning `{}` into `null` — that's incorrect.

maria: actionable: ben, can you open a small PR to change serialization to preserve empty dicts as `{}`? mark as patch, add a unit test asserting outgoing JSON. tag me for review. i'll also add a quick server-side guard to return clearer error message if `metadata` is `null`. that will help customers while SDK patch rolls out.

ben_engineer: will do. PR #4321 drafted. tests failing in CI because codegen snapshot changed — cc @ci-bot for CI run.

ci-bot: build queued for PR #4321 — running unit + serialization tests.

sam_p: also add a tiny doc blurb in sdk-interop.md about map encoding: explicit `{}` must serialize to `{}`, `undefined`/omitted vs `null` semantics. low friction for downstream teams.

alex.g: thanks. small follow-ups: can eng-runtime/validation team relax message to `400 invalid metadata: null` -> `400 invalid metadata: must be object if present`? that will be clearer. maria, can you file a ticket and mention the validation code path?

maria: filing now. ticket INF-987, linking PR and test vectors.

ben_engineer: PR up: 1712345678/4321 — changes serializer and adds test asserting body contains \"metadata\": {} when input is {}. pinging @maria for review.

alex.g: perfect. thanks all :thumbsup:

sam_p: will follow up in eng-platform weekly notes so SDK maintainers are aware.

ci-bot: PR #4321 — all tests passed (serialization unit tests included). merge ready.

alex.g: merging once maria approves. if anyone wants to test locally: curl + example payloads below: 
```bash
# expect 200
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/predict -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input":"x","metadata":{}}'
# expect 400 for null
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/predict -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input":"x","metadata":null}'
```

maria: reviewed and approved. merging now. INF-987 updated to "validation: improve null metadata error message".

alex.g: resolved, closing thread.
